main_text.p: propheta prædicit: Væ Terra umbræ alarum, quæ est ultra flumina Cusch. Hic doctissimis interpretibus, Hebræis & aliis placet, Troglodytarum terram proprie intelligi: quæ pellitur umbrosa alis, ob navium & velorum obumbrantium frequentiam, quæ id navibus præstant, quod alæ avibus. Nam naves, quum earum vela ventis impulsa sunt, per maria quasi volitant. Hinc Chaldæus Paraphrastes: Et vela eorum extenta sicut aquilarum volitantium. Sensus ergo: O terra multis mercatoriarum navium velis, quasi avium alis obumbrata, quanquâ [?] & Terra umbræ alarum dici possit; quia umbræ ejus sint quasi alæ atque pennigeræ; quippe quia post sol stitiu statim avolent. Nam, quod ἀξιομνημόνευτόν [?] ἐστιν [?], in Berenice & Ptolemaide, quæ duo olim principes fuerunt Troglodytarum urbes, ante solstitium XLV diebus, totidemque postea, nullam umbram jaci, atque adeoLi.6. e.24 [?] in tota Troglodytica hisce XLV diebus umbram contrariam cadere, Plinius Eratosthenis testimonio confirmat. Vel certè magis ἁπλῶς [?] dici potest Terra umbræ alarum; quia videlicet in universum umbræ ejus sint quasi alatæ, hoc est, raræ, momentaneæ, fugaces, & citissimè avolantes. Vel etiam divisis dictionibus, forsan primò dicitur Terra umbræ, admirabilis videlicet umbræ,

The Greek words are copied as far as they are legible at this scan resolution, and their accents are uncertain. "quanquâ" is doubtful. The first word "Væ" carries an æ ligature; read as "Væ". The running head is at the top of the page. Lines start without indentation, so the text is one paragraph. The first word continues from the previous page.
